thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty autopage fired for node rc-rack-12-node-49 (gpu-host) — metric: heartbeat_missing, count=3, severity=high. PD incident: INC-84219.

oncall-ops: saw the page. pinging serial console now.

Alice Chen: acked. I'm taking this — will triage. assigning to @Mateo for power/serial help.

Mateo Rivera: on it. can you confirm pods on node? I'll try getting serial attach.

Priya Singh: tagging customer-impact channel — quick check: any customer-facing jobs pinned to this node?

Alice Chen: `kubectl get pods --all-namespaces -o wide --field-selector spec.nodeName=rc-rack-12-node-49` shows ~10 pods, mostly db-backed workers, 2 realtime-infer replicas. No critical LB pinned.

Alice Chen: node status from last scrape: `Ready: Unknown, Kubelet: NotReady, LastHeartbeat: 2023-11-03T14:02:31Z`, kernel logs indicate nvme I/O errors around that time.

Mateo Rivera: serial attached. console showing repeated kernel stack traces, then silent. can't send input. Attempting IPMI power cycle as soft reboot.

incident-bot: PagerDuty update: INC-84219 escalated to on-call-manager after 5m no-ack by responder.

Alice Chen: acknowledged earlier so PD should be satisfied. I'm starting drain plan: cordon first, then `kubectl drain rc-rack-12-node-49 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force` for the realtime pods. Will monitor rollout.

Priya Singh: customer-impact quick check: two customers (acct: bluebird-ai, acct: juno-analytics) have inference traffic that could be routed away. recommending rate-limit fallback and re-route to regional pool. tagging infra-networking. :white_check_mark:

Mateo Rivera: IPMI soft powercycle completed, node came back to BIOS POST, fans spun. Boot stalls at kernel init with nvme reset loops. attaching dmesg snippet:
```
[  11.243] nvme0: I/O 0x3 failed, status: 0x4, info: 0x0
[  11.246] nvme0: Reset controller due to error
[  11.247] Kernel panic - not syncing: Attempted to kill init! exitcode=0x0000000b
```

Alice Chen: oh that's nasty. looks like an NVMe controller fault. RMA likely but we need live mitigation.

oncall-ops: suggest marking node unschedulable in cluster autoscaler config to avoid rescheduling there until fixed.

Alice Chen: done: `kubectl label node rc-rack-12-node-49 redwood/maintenance=true` and `kubectl annotate node rc-rack-12-node-49 redwood/maintenance_reason=nvme_io`

Mateo Rivera: proposing fallback path: spin up 2 replacement workers in the same zone using reserved pool (dedicated: small-gpu-spot-2), then shift traffic using route weights. Priya, can you coordinate with traffic team?

Priya Singh: started change with trafficops: raising weight on replacement pool by 30%, lowering rc-rack-12 weight. will monitor 5m windows. posting links to dashboards.

incident-bot: Note: automatic remediation attempt — kubelet-restart script triggered but failed due to kernel panic.

Alice Chen: manual steps for now: drain complete, pods evicted. No pod restarts stuck. Customer-impact minimal: transient 503s for one tenant for ~2m during evict. Logged in incident timeline.

Mateo Rivera: opened RMA ticket with hosting: RMA-1298, included serial: SN: RCK12-49-8F9. ETA on replacement SSD 72h. Will keep node offline.

Alice Chen: creating a short postmortem stub. Key notes: nvme controller failure -> kernel panic -> kubelet not ready -> PD autopage tripped -> oncall drain+evac -> replacement pool and traffic shift -> RMA.

Priya Singh: leaving monitoring alerts at elevated sensitivity for 24h across the rack to detect sibling failures. config: alert: nvme_io_rate (>5 errors in 1m), kubelet_not_ready (>2m).

Mateo Rivera: leaving a playbook snippet in ops-runbook channel for similar cases. small checklist: serial attach -> ipmi softpower -> collect dmesg -> if nvme loops -> cordon+drain -> spin replacement -> RMA.

Alice Chen: handing off to @Mateo for long tail and hardware followup. I'll mark this thread as incident-handled for now. :white_check_mark: Reaction: +1

Mateo Rivera: thanks — I'll keep the node object tainted and update RMA status here. closing on-call handoff at 6832101600.

incident-bot: INC-84219 status: acknowledged -> mitigated -> monitoring.

Alice Chen: final note: do we want an immediate eval to see whether batching or caching config reduced customer impact? quick check later.

Priya Singh: will run a short traffic replay against replaced pool to validate perf tomorrow morning.
